card.name: Linking words in early church history
card.fires_on: Small linking words and commas (of, and, with, a comma) just before a name or date in text about late-antique popes, emperors and church writers.

modes.label: Of or and before a name
modes.description: The word 'of' or 'and' sits right before a person or people in early Christian or Roman history.
modes.example: It fell during the stormy times<< of>> the Lombard invasion, and practically all

modes.label: Title or comma before a ruler or author
modes.description: A title like Emperor, or a comma in a list of church historians, comes just before the next name.
modes.example: the Virgin Mary appeared to<< Emperor>> Justinian first as a beautiful gazelle

card.writes: It seems to push the model toward ancient-history names and dates, such as 'BC' and Chinese character forms, over other continuations.
card.plain: It fires on little connecting words in writing about early popes and Roman emperors, just before the next name or date.
